2. Heard Sri Janardan Yadav, learned counsel for the applicants and Sri Rajesh Kumar, learned counsel for the informant as well as Ms. Ifra Islam, learned A.G.A. for the State and also perused the material available on record.

3. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicants in Case Crime No. 76 of 2017, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC, Police Station Bilariyaganj, District Azamgarh, with a prayer to enlarge them on anticipatory bail.

sentences.text:
As per prosecution story, the applicants are stated to have got the names entered in the house of the informant in collusion with the Head Clerk Rafi Ullah of Nagar Panchayat, District Bilariyaganj,
District Azamgarh and had got the name of the informant deleted from the records.
5.
Learned counsel for the applicants has stated that the applicants are maliciously being prosecuted in the present case due to ulterior motive and have the apprehension of their arrest.
The applicants have nothing to do with the said offence as alleged by the prosecution and they are the bonafide persons.
Learned counsel has next stated that there was the illegality committed by the Clerk regarding the parentage of applicant no. 2.
It is next stated that the applicant had moved an application for getting the name of informant entered in the records, as it had been removed inadvertently.
It is stated that the family feud has been converted to criminal one in the instant case.
The case, if any, is of civil nature.
6. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicants to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against them.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicants have also been touched upon at length.
It is further submitted that the applicants have criminal history of two cases, which have also been instituted by the same informant and they have been foisted subsequent to the instant case.
In case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicants is allowed, they will not misuse the liberty and shall cooperate with trial.

7. On the other hand, learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the informant have vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicants.

8. On due consideration to the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and considering the nature of accusations and antecedents of the applicants, the applicants are liable to be enlarged on anticipatory bail, in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1".

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The future contingencies regarding the anticipatory bail being granted to applicant shall also be taken care of as per the aforesaid judgement of the Apex Court.
9. Without expressing any opinion upon ultimate merits of the case either ways which may adversely affect the trial of the case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicants is allowed.

sentences.text: 11. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicants.

12. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicants shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
